content: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a guideline in 2017 on school health services, providing comprehensive recommendations for improving health services within educational institutions. 2. In 2021, WHO released the Life Skills Education School Handbook – Noncommunicable Diseases: Approaches for Schools, which outlines strategies for schools to address noncommunicable diseases through life skills education. 3. WHO and UNAIDS developed Global Standards for Quality Health-Care Services for Adolescents, a guide to implementing a standards-driven approach to enhance the quality of healthcare services for adolescents. Volume 1 focuses on the standards and criteria necessary for this improvement. 4. Volume 2 of the same guide provides an implementation manual, detailing the steps required to apply these standards effectively in healthcare settings for adolescents. 5. Volume 3 of the guide offers tools to conduct quality and coverage measurement surveys, enabling the collection of data on compliance with the global standards for adolescent healthcare services. 6. WHO has also published Making Every School a Health-Promoting School: Implementation Guidance, which provides actionable steps for schools to adopt health-promoting practices. 7. The WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific documented experiences from the region in implementing health-promoting schools, offering insights and lessons learned. 8. The WHO Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean conducted a consultation in 2005 on health-promoting schools in the region, addressing regional challenges and opportunities. 9. A report on cost-effective approaches to improving global learning highlights evidence-based smart buys for enhancing education outcomes in lowand middle-income countries. 10. WHO developed an assessment tool to conduct a gap analysis against global standards for health-promoting schools, helping institutions identify areas for improvement. 11. The School Health Profiles tool provides a framework for assessing and monitoring the health status and needs of schools. 12. The Physical Education Curriculum Analysis Tool is designed to evaluate the quality and comprehensiveness of physical education programs in schools. 13. The Health Education Curriculum Analysis Tool (HECAT) supports the evaluation and improvement of health education curricula to ensure alignment with best practices. 14. The School Health Index is a self-assessment and planning guide that includes an e-learning module to help schools evaluate and enhance their health-related policies and programs. 15. The Rapid Assessment and Action Planning Process is a WHO tool designed to facilitate quick evaluations and the development of actionable plans for improving school health initiatives. 16. Annex 2 of the WHO document provides additional resources and tools to support the implementation of health-promoting school strategies.
